questions.question_text:
A pattern has $10$ dots in each group and one group per stage.
Which row completes stages $1$, $2$, $3$?

options.why: Adds $1$ dot per stage instead of adding another group of $10$.
Adds the stage number to $10$ instead of multiplying groups by dots per group.
Multiplies each previous count by $10$ instead of adding one equal group.

questions.question_text:
A pattern has as many strips as its stage number, and each strip has $17$ tiles.
What is the table entry for stage $4$?

options.why: Adds the stage number to $17$ instead of using four groups of $17$.
Uses only three groups of $17$, so the table is one stage behind.
Reverses the digits of the correct product rather than recording $4 \times 17$.

questions.question_text:
A design has $19$ pegs per frame and as many frames as its stage number.
Which pair belongs in the stage-$3$ column?

options.why: Adds $3$ to $19$ instead of counting three equal frames.
Counts only two frames of $19$, leaving the table one stage short.
Swaps the stage number and item count instead of keeping their roles.

questions.question_text:
A pattern has as many sections as its stage number, with $20$ beads per section.
What is the bead count in the stage-$7$ column of its table?

options.why: Adds $7$ to $20$ instead of counting seven sections of $20$ beads.
Counts six sections of $20$ beads instead of seven.
Counts eight sections of $20$ beads instead of seven.

questions.question_text:
A pattern has as many groups as its stage number, with $21$ counters per group. Its table shows stage $2$ as $42$.
What count should appear at stage $6$?

options.why: Adds four to $42$ for the stage gap instead of using six full groups.
Adds another $42$ once, which gives stage $4$ rather than stage $6$.
Multiplies the stage-$2$ count by $6$ instead of scaling it by $6 \div 2$.

questions.question_text:
A pattern uses $22$ lights per panel.
Which row completes the table for $2$, $4$, $6$ and $8$ panels?

options.why: Adds each number of panels to $22$ instead of multiplying it by $22$.
Starts with the correct count for two panels but adds only $2$ lights for each additional pair of panels.
Adds only one panel's $22$ lights between columns although the number of panels increases by $2$.
